dimensions.label: Competent, independent, impartial tribunal established by law
dimensions.standard: The adjudicating tribunal must be competent, independent, impartial and established by law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Determination of a criminal charge or rights/obligations in a suit at law.
dimensions.exceptions: An adverse ruling alone does not establish bias. Assess special/military proceedings and law establishing jurisdiction; core independence/impartiality cannot be displaced by convenience.
questions: What law establishes the tribunal's authority?

dimensions.applicability: Determination of a criminal charge or rights/obligations in a suit at law. An adverse ruling alone does not establish bias. Assess special/military proceedings and law establishing jurisdiction; core independence/impartiality cannot be displaced by convenience.

dimensions.label: Equality before courts and equality of arms
dimensions.standard: Equality before courts and tribunals requires equal access and procedural opportunities; distinctions require objective, reasonable justification without actual disadvantage or unfairness.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Court/tribunal access and relevant proceedings, including criminal charges and suits at law.
dimensions.exceptions: Different treatment is not automatically unlawful; examine objective reasons, actual disadvantage and access barriers. Do not equate equal arms with identical roles.
questions: Could the parties access the tribunal and make submissions?
Did disclosure, resources or procedure put one party at material disadvantage, with what justification?
dimensions.applicability: Court/tribunal access and relevant proceedings, including criminal charges and suits at law. Different treatment is not automatically unlawful; examine objective reasons, actual disadvantage and access barriers. Do not equate equal arms with identical roles.

dimensions.label: Public hearings and public judgments
dimensions.standard: Hearings and judgments must ordinarily be public; permitted exclusions and judgment exceptions require case-specific justification.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.

Was the judgment made public, subject to applicable exceptions?

dimensions.label: Presumption of innocence
dimensions.standard: Everyone charged with a criminal offence is presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law; the prosecution bears the burden and authorities must refrain from prejudging guilt.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through adjudication.
dimensions.exceptions: Prosecution, detention or an adverse verdict alone does not establish failure; distinguish official statements and presentation from a properly reached finding.
questions: Who bore the burden and what proof standard was used?
Did authorities prejudge guilt or present the accused as guilty?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge through adjudication. Prosecution, detention or an adverse verdict alone does not establish failure; distinguish official statements and presentation from a properly reached finding.

dimensions.label: Notice of charges
dimensions.standard: Prompt, detailed notice in a language understood of the nature and cause of the criminal charge.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge, rather than only preliminary investigation before charges.
dimensions.exceptions: Arrest reasons under Article 9 are a distinct related guarantee; formal notice must address law and alleged general facts, orally or in writing as appropriate.
questions: When did the person learn the charge and alleged acts?
What details and language were provided?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge, rather than only preliminary investigation before charges. Arrest reasons under Article 9 are a distinct related guarantee; formal notice must address law and alleged general facts, orally or in writing as appropriate.

dimensions.label: Adequate time and facilities for defence
dimensions.standard: Adequate time and facilities to prepare the defence, including access to relevant documents and other evidence needed for defence.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Preparation for a criminal charge, hearings and relevant defence steps.
dimensions.exceptions: Adequacy depends on complexity, access and circumstances. Requests for additional time and reasoned rulings matter; document volume alone is not adequacy.
questions: What preparation time, case complexity and disclosure were available?
Were necessary adjournments/access requested and how were requests decided?
dimensions.applicability: Preparation for a criminal charge, hearings and relevant defence steps. Adequacy depends on complexity, access and circumstances. Requests for additional time and reasoned rulings matter; document volume alone is not adequacy.

dimensions.label: Access to effective legal assistance
dimensions.standard: Defence in person or through legal assistance of choice, confidential access to counsel, and assigned effective assistance where justice requires subject to means conditions.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal defence; distinguish custodial/investigation guarantees under Article 9 and applicable domestic law.
dimensions.exceptions: Assigned assistance depends on interests of justice and lack of means for free assistance. Self-representation restrictions require objective sufficiently serious reasons; attributed counsel errors require case-specific responsibility analysis.
questions: Was counsel chosen/assigned, accessible and confidential?

Assigned assistance depends on interests of justice and lack of means for free assistance. Self-representation restrictions require objective sufficiently serious reasons; attributed counsel errors require case-specific responsibility analysis.

dimensions.label: Presence and meaningful participation
dimensions.standard: An accused ordinarily has a right to be tried in their presence and meaningfully defend the case.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal trial and defence participation.
dimensions.exceptions: Proceedings in absence can be permissible in specific circumstances after sufficient notice and opportunity; verify steps informing the accused and justification, not absence alone.
questions: Was the accused present, informed and able to follow/respond?
If absent or restricted, what notice/opportunity and reasons existed?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal trial and defence participation. Proceedings in absence can be permissible in specific circumstances after sufficient notice and opportunity; verify steps informing the accused and justification, not absence alone.

dimensions.label: Examine witnesses and present defence evidence
dimensions.standard: Examine prosecution witnesses and obtain/examine defence witnesses under the same conditions; meaningful opportunity to challenge material evidence.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal trial and material defence evidence requests.
dimensions.exceptions: This is not an unlimited right to call every witness. Identify relevance, requests, refusals, reasons and disadvantage.
questions: Could material prosecution witnesses/evidence be challenged?
Could relevant defence witnesses/evidence be presented under comparable conditions?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal trial and material defence evidence requests. This is not an unlimited right to call every witness. Identify relevance, requests, refusals, reasons and disadvantage.

dimensions.label: Interpretation where required
dimensions.standard: Free assistance of an interpreter where the accused cannot understand or speak the language used in court.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings when courtroom language cannot be understood/spoken.

questions: What language ability and proceedings language are documented?

dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings when courtroom language cannot be understood/spoken. Nationality or multilingual setting alone does not prove need or adequacy. This right does not require proceedings in the preferred language where the court language is sufficiently understood.

dimensions.label: Protection against compelled self-incrimination
dimensions.standard: No compulsion to testify against oneself or confess guilt; exclude prohibited coercion and examine allegations of involuntary statements.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial.
dimensions.exceptions: Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.
questions: How was the statement obtained and was compulsion alleged?
How did the court handle coercion allegations and use/exclusion?
dimensions.applicability: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial. Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.

dimensions.label: Trial without undue delay
dimensions.standard: Criminal proceedings must proceed without undue delay, assessed from formal charge through final judgment including appeal.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal.
dimensions.exceptions: Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.
questions: What intervals, procedural steps and reasons for delay are documented?
How do complexity, party conduct, court conduct and detention affect adequacy?

dimensions.label: Review of conviction and sentence
dimensions.standard: Conviction and sentence must be reviewed by a higher tribunal according to law, including sufficient substantive review of facts and law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review.
dimensions.exceptions: Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.
questions: Was higher review available and effective for both conviction and sentence?
What facts/law, judgment and record were reviewed and what barriers existed?
dimensions.applicability: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review. Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.

dimensions.label: Conditional juvenile safeguards
dimensions.standard: Proceedings for juveniles must take account of age and the desirability of promoting rehabilitation.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date.
dimensions.exceptions: Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.
questions: What age/status applies at the event date?
What age-appropriate procedure, assistance and rehabilitation/diversion protections were used?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date. Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.

dimensions.label: Conditional protection from double jeopardy
dimensions.standard: No repeated trial or punishment for an offence after final conviction/acquittal under the law and penal procedure of the same country.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence.
dimensions.exceptions: Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. Higher review and narrowly justified resumption on exceptional grounds are distinct; the Covenant does not automatically prohibit prosecutions in different national jurisdictions.
questions: Was a prior decision final, for the same offence in the same country?
Is this a new prosecution or permitted review/resumption, on what grounds?
dimensions.applicability: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence. Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. dimensions.label: Conditional miscarriage-of-justice compensation

dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction.
dimensions.exceptions: Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. Examine final conviction, punishment, newly discovered fact, conclusive miscarriage and whether non-disclosure was wholly/partly attributable to the person.
questions: Do final conviction, punishment, qualifying reversal/pardon and new fact meet the conditions?
What compensation route and non-disclosure exception apply?
dimensions.applicability: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction. Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial.
dimensions.exceptions: Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.
questions: How was the statement obtained and was compulsion alleged?
How did the court handle coercion allegations and use/exclusion?
dimensions.applicability: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial. Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.

dimensions.label: Trial without undue delay
dimensions.standard: Criminal proceedings must proceed without undue delay, assessed from formal charge through final judgment including appeal.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal.
dimensions.exceptions: Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.
questions: What intervals, procedural steps and reasons for delay are documented?
How do complexity, party conduct, court conduct and detention affect adequacy?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal. Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.

dimensions.label: Review of conviction and sentence
dimensions.standard: Conviction and sentence must be reviewed by a higher tribunal according to law, including sufficient substantive review of facts and law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review.
dimensions.exceptions: Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.
questions: Was higher review available and effective for both conviction and sentence?
What facts/law, judgment and record were reviewed and what barriers existed?
dimensions.applicability: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review. Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.

dimensions.label: Conditional juvenile safeguards
dimensions.standard: Proceedings for juveniles must take account of age and the desirability of promoting rehabilitation.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date.
dimensions.exceptions: Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.
questions: What age/status applies at the event date?
What age-appropriate procedure, assistance and rehabilitation/diversion protections were used?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date. Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.

dimensions.label: Conditional protection from double jeopardy
dimensions.standard: No repeated trial or punishment for an offence after final conviction/acquittal under the law and penal procedure of the same country.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence.
dimensions.exceptions: Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. Higher review and narrowly justified resumption on exceptional grounds are distinct; the Covenant does not automatically prohibit prosecutions in different national jurisdictions.
questions: Was a prior decision final, for the same offence in the same country?
Is this a new prosecution or permitted review/resumption, on what grounds?
dimensions.applicability: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence. Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. Higher review and narrowly justified resumption on exceptional grounds are distinct; the Covenant does not automatically prohibit prosecutions in different national jurisdictions.

dimensions.label: Conditional miscarriage-of-justice compensation
dimensions.standard: Compensation according to law where a final conviction is reversed or a pardon granted because a new/newly discovered fact conclusively shows miscarriage of justice, subject to non-disclosure conditions.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction.
dimensions.exceptions: Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. Examine final conviction, punishment, newly discovered fact, conclusive miscarriage and whether non-disclosure was wholly/partly attributable to the person.
questions: Do final conviction, punishment, qualifying reversal/pardon and new fact meet the conditions?
What compensation route and non-disclosure exception apply?
dimensions.applicability: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction. Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. Examine final conviction, punishment, newly discovered fact, conclusive miscarriage and whether non-disclosure was wholly/partly attributable to the person.

dimensions.label: Expression and restrictive interference
dimensions.standard: Identify the expression, whether Article 19 protects it and the specific restriction. Freedom to hold opinions without interference is distinct from expression restrictions.
dimensions.applicability: Do not presume expression was involved in every prosecution. Identify conduct and restriction; Article 20 duties and other rights may also require analysis.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR Article 19 and relevant domestic law at the event date.
dimensions.stage: Identified expression and interference/restriction, including prosecution where linked.
dimensions.exceptions: Do not presume expression was involved in every prosecution. Identify conduct and restriction; Article 20 duties and other rights may also require analysis.

dimensions.label: Restriction's legal basis
dimensions.standard: Any restriction of protected expression must be provided by law with sufficient precision and accessible guidance; discretion must be bounded.
dimensions.applicability: First establish expression and restriction. Citation of a statute alone does not settle foreseeability or its application.

dimensions.applicability: Assess actual expression, aim, harm, penalty and alternatives. A restriction is not automatically unlawful; a legal basis and aim do not automatically establish necessity.

missing_facts: RTC establishment/jurisdiction law and judicial appointment/conflict facts not inspected.
Original warrant order and any judicial recusal record absent.
dimensions.explanation: The Court reports reliance on the prosecutor certification instead of personal evidence evaluation, and PACC involvement in the preliminary inquiry. That documented warrant failure is separately retained under Article 9 and Constitution III.2. It does not by itself establish unlawful tribunal establishment, jurisdictional incompetence, institutional dependence or personal bias. The replacement prosecutor panel and effective Supreme Court intervention qualify the institutional account. An adverse or legally erroneous decision alone is not a tribunal-independence finding.
dimensions.next_verification: Inspect a specific tribunal establishment, independence or impartiality proposition before assigning a score; do not transfer prosecutor affiliation to the judge.
dimensions.applicability: Criminal-charge and judicial warrant-review context, 1993-1994; prosecutorial investigation and judicial adjudication are distinct.

missing_facts: Original affidavits, disclosure inventory, panel orders and hearing transcripts absent.
Any lawful justification or earlier opportunity to answer Bato not fully documented beyond the judgment.
dimensions.explanation: Anchor 2: substantial documented procedural disadvantage. Requested documents were reportedly not supplied despite an order; the Court expressly states that Bato counter-affidavit was considered without an opportunity for petitioners to refute it. That late material supported the information and ensuing warrant. Some affidavits were disclosed, the panel was replaced, a warrant opposition was allowed and later judicial relief succeeded. Those qualifications do not establish a contemporaneous opportunity to answer the late material before the challenged decision. This provisional analysis overlaps disclosure facts in preparation_facilities and must not be summed with them.
dimensions.next_verification: A qualified reviewer should confirm the late-evidence chronology and how the disadvantage persisted into the post-charge judicial decision.
dimensions.applicability: Article 14(1) fairness/equality in the described criminal-charge process; the clearest direct finding concerns preliminary-investigation material used for the later warrant.

missing_facts: Public access arrangements, any exclusion order and contemporaneous public-release information absent.
dimensions.explanation: A Supreme Court hearing and reasoned disposition are documented. The retained online reproduction does not establish whether the 1994 hearing was open, when the judgment was publicly released, or whether any exclusion was justified. Radio coverage and current web availability are not event-time public-access evidence.
dimensions.next_verification: Inspect authorized hearing/publication records; do not infer publicity from news or an online copy.
dimensions.applicability: Stage-specific judicial review of a pretrial warrant; no merits trial documented, and not every pretrial step requires a public hearing.

missing_facts: Original context and public dissemination of official statements absent.
No guilt trial, burden instructions or accused-presentation record.
dimensions.explanation: Lacson letter is recounted as an accusation, and the Court criticizes prosecutorial eagerness. A charging allegation or disputed probable-cause decision alone is not proof of official prejudgment or reversal of the trial burden. The State offered a probable-cause position; the Court rejected it without conducting a guilt trial. No trial burden instructions or presentation record is supplied.
dimensions.next_verification: Review the original charging context and any public statements before distinguishing allegation from prohibited prejudgment.
dimensions.applicability: Charged persons in 1993-1994; probable cause and proof of guilt perform different functions.

missing_facts: Subpoena service date, original information and each petitioner language comprehension absent.
Event-time procedural trigger needs qualified review.
dimensions.explanation: The judgment records a subpoena with affidavits and procurement of the information on 3 February 1994, the day filed, plus a runaround obtaining the resolution and information. It supports a notice/disclosure question but not a demonstrated delayed or unintelligible charge: service dates, full charge and language comprehension are missing. Contemporary GC13 paragraph 8 describes a procedural/public-naming notice trigger; later GC32 paragraph 31 describes a formal-charge trigger. That difference is retained rather than silently applying the later formulation to 1993.
dimensions.next_verification: Inspect subpoena/information and service records, separating charge notice from arrest reasons and later disclosure.
dimensions.applicability: Article 14(3)(a); investigation, public naming and February 1994 information are distinct; GC32 is later interpretive guidance.

missing_facts: Complete disclosure inventory, original production/ruling documents and any privilege/nonexistence explanation absent.
Preparation communications and complete actual prejudice not documented.
dimensions.explanation: Anchor 2: substantial documented concern on defence facilities. Mendoza requested identified documents for an intelligible counter-affidavit; the replacement panel ordered production, yet requested material was not supplied and a late implicating affidavit was used before petitioners could refute it. GC13 paragraph 9, adopted in 1984, addresses defence-needed documents. Later opportunity to oppose a warrant and judicial relief are safeguards but do not show adequate access at the earlier consequential decision. Missing original file and limited historical phase make level 3 unwarranted; no irreversible trial disadvantage is invented.
dimensions.next_verification: Distinguish material existing, requested and withheld; review the precharge/postcharge consequence using event-time procedure, not the 2000 Rules.
dimensions.applicability: Defence preparation around preliminary investigation, information and warrant. Domestic due-process reasoning supports stage relevance; no unlimited access right is asserted.

missing_facts: Counsel access during surrender/custody, confidential consultation and all-stage quality absent.
No indigence or assignment issue established.
dimensions.explanation: Anchor 0, narrowly scoped: affirmative evidence documents access to named counsel and a functioning defence challenge in this warrant-review phase. Salonga is counsel; oppositions, DOJ review and Supreme Court interim/final relief are recorded. Representation/access is the documented safeguard. Being lawyers themselves does not eliminate counsel needs. Confidentiality, custodial access, means and all-stage quality remain unverified; this is not whole-proceeding legal-assistance certification.
dimensions.next_verification: Confirm counsel access and any custody consultation limits before expanding this dimension beyond the documented judicial challenge.
dimensions.applicability: Articles 14(3)(b),(d) assistance in the warrant challenge; zero rests on identified counsel and actual defence steps, not missing allegations.

missing_facts: Individual attendance, oral participation and any reasoned absence restriction absent.
No merits-trial record.
dimensions.explanation: Written submissions, objections and a Supreme Court hearing show participation opportunities; late adverse material was not answerable at the earlier decision. Individual presence, ability to follow oral proceedings and a merits trial are not established. The response deficit is assessed under equality/preparation, not converted into a trial-presence finding.
dimensions.next_verification: Inspect authorized attendance/hearing records before assessing personal trial presence or oral participation.
dimensions.applicability: Defence participation relevant; trial-presence components not shown by a pretrial writ proceeding.

missing_facts: Witness/evidence requests, rulings, comparable powers and full hearing transcript absent.
dimensions.explanation: The Court examined inconsistent witness accounts and the late affidavit. The record does not identify examination/defence-witness requests refused or allowed under comparable conditions. Full preliminary-hearing cross-examination and a merits trial are absent. The lost response opportunity supports equality/preparation but alone does not establish a distinct witness-examination score.
dimensions.next_verification: Identify exact relevant requests/refusals and reasons before assigning an independent score.
dimensions.applicability: Article 14(3)(e) material evidence opportunities; clarificatory preliminary questions are not automatically trial cross-examination.

missing_facts: Language ability, proceeding language and interpretation needs/requests absent.
dimensions.explanation: The persons are practising lawyers and the reproduction is English. Neither proves they understood all proceedings or had no interpreter need. No need, request or provision is recorded; missingness cannot yield zero or categorical not-applicable.
dimensions.next_verification: Verify event-time language need from records; do not infer it from nationality, profession or source language.
dimensions.applicability: Article 14(3)(f) conditional on ability to understand/speak the oral-proceeding language; trigger unknown.

missing_facts: Original Bato affidavit, suppression motion and coercion investigation absent.
No compelled petitioner statement or authoritative coercion finding established.
dimensions.explanation: Bato, a co-accused whose statement was used against petitioners, reportedly alleged duress and sought suppression. The Court discounted its probative value. This is not an authenticated torture finding or a compelled confession by Allado/Mendoza, who submitted denials. Allegedly coerced material raises a separate fairness/Article 7 issue; no personal Article 14(3)(g) score transfers from Bato to these petitioners.
dimensions.next_verification: Keep identities separate; inspect voluntariness/exclusion records before assessing Bato own right or statement use against others.
dimensions.applicability: Articles 14(3)(g),7: personal self-incrimination distinct from general fairness in use of co-accused material.

missing_facts: Interval reasons and complete procedural/custody records absent.
Impossible release date unresolved.
dimensions.explanation: Some steps run from September 1993 to the May 1994 writ disposition; the Court criticizes haste, not a prolonged trial. No full criminal chronology, interval reasons or reliable custody duration is supplied. JP0021 states release on 29 February 1994, an impossible date, retained verbatim with no silent correction or detention-day count. Chronology cannot support a delay score or zero.
dimensions.next_verification: Resolve the date against authorized original records and inspect interval reasons; elapsed time alone is insufficient.
dimensions.applicability: Article 14(3)(c) charge process; investigation and Article 9 prompt judicial control retain distinct standards.

missing_facts: No claim about proceedings outside this document.
dimensions.explanation: DOJ review and certiorari/prohibition are pretrial remedies. The Court sets aside a warrant and enjoins proceedings; it does not review a conviction/sentence. Article 14(5) is not triggered in this bounded phase. Effective pretrial relief stays separately recorded.
dimensions.next_verification: Reopen only when a distinct conviction/sentence and higher review are supplied.
dimensions.applicability: Article 14(5) requires conviction/sentence; this is pretrial warrant review.

dimensions.explanation: Practising-lawyer status suggests adulthood but no event-time ages are explicitly supplied. Dates of birth are not invented, and unverified trigger facts are not automatically classified not-applicable.
dimensions.next_verification: Verify age/status if relevant before deciding applicability.
dimensions.applicability: Article 14(4) conditional age/status trigger remains unverified.

missing_facts: Finality and later same-offence proceedings outside this phase unknown.
dimensions.explanation: The bounded phase describes an initial information and pretrial challenge, not later prosecution after a final conviction/acquittal. Quashing a warrant is not silently transformed into merits acquittal or an occurring second prosecution.
dimensions.next_verification: Reopen on a supplied final merits disposition and distinct later same-offence proceeding; verify domestic rules first.
dimensions.applicability: No Article 14(7) repeat-prosecution trigger in the described phase; no global claim about other proceedings.

dimensions.explanation: Pretrial warrant relief does not satisfy Article 14(6) final conviction, punishment and qualifying new-fact reversal/pardon conditions. Possible Article 9(5) unlawful-arrest compensation is separate and no domestic entitlement is inferred.
dimensions.next_verification: Reopen on the qualifying Article 14(6) sequence, not merely warrant set-aside.
dimensions.applicability: Article 14(6) not triggered by the documented pretrial writ relief.

However, we are unable to see how respondent judge arrived at such ruling. We have painstakingly examined the records and we cannot find any support for his conclusion. On the contrary, we discern a number of reasons why we consider the evidence submitted to be insufficient for a finding of probable cause against petitioners.

claims.excerpt: For sure, the credibility of Umbal is badly battered. Certainly, his bare allegations, even if the State invokes its inherent right to prosecute, are insufficient to justify sending two lawyers to jail, or anybody for that matter. More importantly, the PACC operatives who applied for a warrant to search the dwellings of Santiago never implicated petitioners. In fact they claimed that according to Umbal, it was Santiago, and not petitioners, who masterminded the whole affair.40 While there may be bits of evidence against petitioners' co-accused, i.e., referring to those seized from the dwellings of Santiago, these do not in the least prove petitioners' complicity in the crime charged. Based on the evidence thus far submitted there is nothing indeed, much less is there probable cause, to incriminate petitioners. For them to stand trial and be deprived in the meantime of their liberty, however brief, the law appropriately exacts much more to sustain a warrant for their arrest — facts and circumstances strong enough in themselves to support the belief that they are guilty of a crime that in fact happened. Quite obviously, this has not been met.

claims.excerpt: In People v. Inting,42 we emphasized the important features of the constitutional mandate: (a) The determination of probable cause is a function of the judge; it is not for the provincial fiscal or prosecutor to ascertain. Only the judge and the judge alone makes this determination; (b) The preliminary inquiry made by a prosecutor does not bind the judge. It merely assists him in making the determination of probable cause. The judge does not have to follow what the prosecutor presents to him. By itself, the prosecutor's certification of probable cause is ineffectual. It is the report, the affidavits, the transcript of stenographic notes (if any), and all other supporting documents behind the prosecutor's certification which are material in assisting the judge in his determination of probable cause; and, (c) Judges and prosecutors alike should distinguish the preliminary inquiry which determines probable cause for the issuance of a warrant of arrest from the preliminary investigation proper which ascertains whether the offender should be held for trial or released. Even if the two inquiries be conducted in the course of one and the same proceeding, there should be no confusion about their objectives. The determination of probable cause for the warrant is made by the judge. The preliminary investigation proper — whether or not there is reasonable ground to believe that the accused is guilty of the offense charged and therefore, whether or not he should be subjected to the expense, rigors and embarrassment of trial — is a function of the prosecutor.

claims.excerpt: In the case at bench, the undue haste in the filing of the information and the inordinate interest of the government cannot be ignored. From the gathering of evidence until the termination of the preliminary investigation, it appears that the state prosecutors were overly eager to file the case and secure a warrant for the arrest of the accused without bail and their consequent detention. Umbal's sworn statement is laden with inconsistencies and improbabilities. Bato's counter-affidavit was considered without giving petitioners the opportunity to refute the same. The PACC which gathered the evidence appears to have had a hand in the determination of probable cause in the preliminary inquiry as the undated resolution of the panel not only bears the letterhead of PACC but was also recommended for approval by the head of the PACC Task Force. Then petitioners were given the runaround in securing a copy of the resolution and the information against them.

claims.excerpt: The purpose of a preliminary investigation is to secure the innocent against hasty, malicious and oppressive prosecution, and to protect him from an open and public accusation of crime, from the trouble, expense and anxiety of a public trial, and also to protect the state from useless and expensive trial (Trocio v. Manta, 118 SCRA 241, citing Hashim v. Boncan, 71 Phil. 216). The right to a preliminary investigation is a statutory grant, and to withhold it would be to transgress constitutional due process (People v. Oandasa, 25 SCRA 277). However, in order to satisfy the due process clause it is not enough that the preliminary investigation is conducted in the sense of making sure that the transgressor shall not escape with impunity. A preliminary investigation serves not only for the purposes of the State. More importantly, it is a part of the guarantees of freedom and fair play which are birthrights of all who live in the country. It is therefore imperative upon the fiscal or the judge as the case may be, to relieve the accused from the pain of going thru a trial once it is ascertained that the evidence is insufficient to sustain a prima facie case or that no probable cause exists to form a sufficient belief as to the guilt of the accused (emphasis supplied).

dimensions.label: Competent, independent, impartial tribunal established by law
dimensions.standard: The adjudicating tribunal must be competent, independent, impartial and established by law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Determination of a criminal charge or rights/obligations in a suit at law.
dimensions.exceptions: An adverse ruling alone does not establish bias. Assess special/military proceedings and law establishing jurisdiction; core independence/impartiality cannot be displaced by convenience.
questions: What law establishes the tribunal's authority?
What evidence addresses competence, interference, conflicts or objective appearance of bias?
dimensions.applicability: Determination of a criminal charge or rights/obligations in a suit at law. An adverse ruling alone does not establish bias. Assess special/military proceedings and law establishing jurisdiction; core independence/impartiality cannot be displaced by convenience.

dimensions.label: Equality before courts and equality of arms
dimensions.standard: Equality before courts and tribunals requires equal access and procedural opportunities; distinctions require objective, reasonable justification without actual disadvantage or unfairness.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Court/tribunal access and relevant proceedings, including criminal charges and suits at law.
dimensions.exceptions: Different treatment is not automatically unlawful; examine objective reasons, actual disadvantage and access barriers. Do not equate equal arms with identical roles.
questions: Could the parties access the tribunal and make submissions?
Did disclosure, resources or procedure put one party at material disadvantage, with what justification?
dimensions.applicability: Court/tribunal access and relevant proceedings, including criminal charges and suits at law. Different treatment is not automatically unlawful; examine objective reasons, actual disadvantage and access barriers. Do not equate equal arms with identical roles.

dimensions.label: Public hearings and public judgments
dimensions.standard: Hearings and judgments must ordinarily be public; permitted exclusions and judgment exceptions require case-specific justification.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Hearing and judgment in determination of a criminal charge or suit at law; determine hearing type, as not every pretrial/appeal step requires a public hearing.
dimensions.exceptions: Press/public may be excluded for morals, public order, national security in a democratic society, private lives, or strictly necessary special circumstances where publicity prejudices justice. Judgment exceptions include juvenile interests or matrimonial/child guardianship disputes.
questions: Was the hearing open to the public, and were any exclusions justified?
Was the judgment made public, subject to applicable exceptions?
components: Exception justification; missing web copies are evidence gaps, not proof
dimensions.applicability: Hearing and judgment in determination of a criminal charge or suit at law; determine hearing type, as not every pretrial/appeal step requires a public hearing. Press/public may be excluded for morals, public order, national security in a democratic society, private lives, or strictly necessary special circumstances where publicity prejudices justice. Judgment exceptions include juvenile interests or matrimonial/child guardianship disputes.

dimensions.label: Presumption of innocence
dimensions.standard: Everyone charged with a criminal offence is presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law; the prosecution bears the burden and authorities must refrain from prejudging guilt.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through adjudication.
dimensions.exceptions: Prosecution, detention or an adverse verdict alone does not establish failure; distinguish official statements and presentation from a properly reached finding.
questions: Who bore the burden and what proof standard was used?
Did authorities prejudge guilt or present the accused as guilty?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge through adjudication. Prosecution, detention or an adverse verdict alone does not establish failure; distinguish official statements and presentation from a properly reached finding.

dimensions.label: Notice of charges
dimensions.standard: Prompt, detailed notice in a language understood of the nature and cause of the criminal charge.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge, rather than only preliminary investigation before charges.
dimensions.exceptions: Arrest reasons under Article 9 are a distinct related guarantee; formal notice must address law and alleged general facts, orally or in writing as appropriate.
questions: When did the person learn the charge and alleged acts?
What details and language were provided?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge, rather than only preliminary investigation before charges. Arrest reasons under Article 9 are a distinct related guarantee; formal notice must address law and alleged general facts, orally or in writing as appropriate.

dimensions.label: Adequate time and facilities for defence
dimensions.standard: Adequate time and facilities to prepare the defence, including access to relevant documents and other evidence needed for defence.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Preparation for a criminal charge, hearings and relevant defence steps.
dimensions.exceptions: Adequacy depends on complexity, access and circumstances. Requests for additional time and reasoned rulings matter; document volume alone is not adequacy.
questions: What preparation time, case complexity and disclosure were available?
Were necessary adjournments/access requested and how were requests decided?
dimensions.applicability: Preparation for a criminal charge, hearings and relevant defence steps. Adequacy depends on complexity, access and circumstances. Requests for additional time and reasoned rulings matter; document volume alone is not adequacy.

dimensions.label: Access to effective legal assistance
dimensions.standard: Defence in person or through legal assistance of choice, confidential access to counsel, and assigned effective assistance where justice requires subject to means conditions.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal defence; distinguish custodial/investigation guarantees under Article 9 and applicable domestic law.
dimensions.exceptions: Assigned assistance depends on interests of justice and lack of means for free assistance. Self-representation restrictions require objective sufficiently serious reasons; attributed counsel errors require case-specific responsibility analysis.

dimensions.label: Presence and meaningful participation
dimensions.standard: An accused ordinarily has a right to be tried in their presence and meaningfully defend the case.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal trial and defence participation.
dimensions.exceptions: Proceedings in absence can be permissible in specific circumstances after sufficient notice and opportunity; verify steps informing the accused and justification, not absence alone.

dimensions.label: Examine witnesses and present defence evidence
dimensions.standard: Examine prosecution witnesses and obtain/examine defence witnesses under the same conditions; meaningful opportunity to challenge material evidence.

dimensions.exceptions: This is not an unlimited right to call every witness. Identify relevance, requests, refusals, reasons and disadvantage.

dimensions.label: Interpretation where required
dimensions.standard: Free assistance of an interpreter where the accused cannot understand or speak the language used in court.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings when courtroom language cannot be understood/spoken.

questions: What language ability and proceedings language are documented?

dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings when courtroom language cannot be understood/spoken. Nationality or multilingual setting alone does not prove need or adequacy. This right does not require proceedings in the preferred language where the court language is sufficiently understood.

dimensions.label: Protection against compelled self-incrimination
dimensions.standard: No compulsion to testify against oneself or confess guilt; exclude prohibited coercion and examine allegations of involuntary statements.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial.
dimensions.exceptions: Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.
questions: How was the statement obtained and was compulsion alleged?
How did the court handle coercion allegations and use/exclusion?
dimensions.applicability: Obtaining/use of statements in a criminal process, including earlier investigation where relevant to trial. Voluntary admission is not automatically prohibited. Distinguish Article 7 coercion and Article 9 detention guarantees; evaluate burden and exclusion of alleged coerced statements.

dimensions.label: Trial without undue delay
dimensions.standard: Criminal proceedings must proceed without undue delay, assessed from formal charge through final judgment including appeal.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal.
dimensions.exceptions: Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.
questions: What intervals, procedural steps and reasons for delay are documented?
How do complexity, party conduct, court conduct and detention affect adequacy?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal charge through final adjudication/appeal. Assess complexity, accused conduct and administrative/judicial handling. Elapsed time or a procedural deadline alone does not establish undue delay; custody increases need for expedition.

dimensions.label: Review of conviction and sentence
dimensions.standard: Conviction and sentence must be reviewed by a higher tribunal according to law, including sufficient substantive review of facts and law.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review.
dimensions.exceptions: Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.
questions: Was higher review available and effective for both conviction and sentence?
What facts/law, judgment and record were reviewed and what barriers existed?
dimensions.applicability: After criminal conviction/sentence and relevant higher review. Guarantee is substantive, not merely a formal check. Civil review is not automatically within Article 14(5); examine applicable special procedures and access to reasoned judgment/record.

dimensions.label: Conditional juvenile safeguards
dimensions.standard: Proceedings for juveniles must take account of age and the desirability of promoting rehabilitation.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date.
dimensions.exceptions: Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.
questions: What age/status applies at the event date?
What age-appropriate procedure, assistance and rehabilitation/diversion protections were used?
dimensions.applicability: Criminal proceedings involving a juvenile at the relevant event date. Age and domestic juvenile status require verification. Juvenile-specific procedure/rehabilitation and diversion where appropriate are distinct from assuming identical adult procedure.

dimensions.label: Conditional protection from double jeopardy
dimensions.standard: No repeated trial or punishment for an offence after final conviction/acquittal under the law and penal procedure of the same country.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence.
dimensions.exceptions: Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. Higher review and narrowly justified resumption on exceptional grounds are distinct; the Covenant does not automatically prohibit prosecutions in different national jurisdictions.
questions: Was a prior decision final, for the same offence in the same country?
Is this a new prosecution or permitted review/resumption, on what grounds?
dimensions.applicability: Later criminal proceedings following a potentially final conviction/acquittal for the same offence. Verify finality/same offence/same jurisdiction. Higher review and narrowly justified resumption on exceptional grounds are distinct; the Covenant does not automatically prohibit prosecutions in different national jurisdictions.

dimensions.label: Conditional miscarriage-of-justice compensation
dimensions.standard: Compensation according to law where a final conviction is reversed or a pardon granted because a new/newly discovered fact conclusively shows miscarriage of justice, subject to non-disclosure conditions.
dimensions.jurisdiction: ICCPR framework; assess treaty/domestic law and version applicable to the event date.
dimensions.stage: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction.
dimensions.exceptions: Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. Examine final conviction, punishment, newly discovered fact, conclusive miscarriage and whether non-disclosure was wholly/partly attributable to the person.
questions: Do final conviction, punishment, qualifying reversal/pardon and new fact meet the conditions?
What compensation route and non-disclosure exception apply?
dimensions.applicability: After qualifying reversal/pardon and punishment following final criminal conviction. Ordinary acquittal, dismissal or reversal alone is insufficient. Examine final conviction, punishment, newly discovered fact, conclusive miscarriage and whether non-disclosure was wholly/partly attributable to the person.

claims.excerpt: In People v. Inting,42 we emphasized the important features of the constitutional mandate: (a) The determination of probable cause is a function of the judge; it is not for the provincial fiscal or prosecutor to ascertain. Only the judge and the judge alone makes this determination; (b) The preliminary inquiry made by a prosecutor does not bind the judge. It merely assists him in making the determination of probable cause. The judge does not have to follow what the prosecutor presents to him. By itself, the prosecutor's certification of probable cause is ineffectual. It is the report, the affidavits, the transcript of stenographic notes (if any), and all other supporting documents behind the prosecutor's certification which are material in assisting the judge in his determination of probable cause; and, (c) Judges and prosecutors alike should distinguish the preliminary inquiry which determines probable cause for the issuance of a warrant of arrest from the preliminary investigation proper which ascertains whether the offender should be held for trial or released. Even if the two inquiries be conducted in the course of one and the same proceeding, there should be no confusion about their objectives. The determination of probable cause for the warrant is made by the judge. The preliminary investigation proper — whether or not there is reasonable ground to believe that the accused is guilty of the offense charged and therefore, whether or not he should be subjected to the expense, rigors and embarrassment of trial — is a function of the prosecutor.

Umbal's sworn statement is laden with inconsistencies and improbabilities. Bato's counter-affidavit was considered without giving petitioners the opportunity to refute the same. The PACC which gathered the evidence appears to have had a hand in the determination of probable cause in the preliminary inquiry as the undated resolution of the panel not only bears the letterhead of PACC but was also recommended for approval by the head of the PACC Task Force. claims.excerpt: The purpose of a preliminary investigation is to secure the innocent against hasty, malicious and oppressive prosecution, and to protect him from an open and public accusation of crime, from the trouble, expense and anxiety of a public trial, and also to protect the state from useless and expensive trial (Trocio v. Manta, 118 SCRA 241, citing Hashim v. Boncan, 71 Phil. 216). The right to a preliminary investigation is a statutory grant, and to withhold it would be to transgress constitutional due process (People v. Oandasa, 25 SCRA 277). However, in order to satisfy the due process clause it is not enough that the preliminary investigation is conducted in the sense of making sure that the transgressor shall not escape with impunity. A preliminary investigation serves not only for the purposes of the State. More importantly, it is a part of the guarantees of freedom and fair play which are birthrights of all who live in the country. It is therefore imperative upon the fiscal or the judge as the case may be, to relieve the accused from the pain of going thru a trial once it is ascertained that the evidence is insufficient to sustain a prima facie case or that no probable cause exists to form a sufficient belief as to the guilt of the accused (emphasis supplied).

missing_facts: Subpoena service date, original information and each petitioner language comprehension absent.

It supports a notice/disclosure question but not a demonstrated delayed or unintelligible charge: service dates, full charge and language comprehension are missing. dimensions.explanation: Anchor 0, narrowly scoped: affirmative evidence documents access to named counsel and a functioning defence challenge in this warrant-review phase. More importantly, the PACC operatives who applied for a warrant to search the dwellings of Santiago never implicated petitioners. In fact they claimed that according to Umbal, it was Santiago, and not petitioners, who masterminded the whole affair.40 While there may be bits of evidence against petitioners' co-accused, i.e., referring to those seized from the dwellings of Santiago, these do not in the least prove petitioners' complicity in the crime charged. Based on the evidence thus far submitted there is nothing indeed, much less is there probable cause, to incriminate petitioners. For them to stand trial and be deprived in the meantime of their liberty, however brief, the law appropriately exacts much more to sustain a warrant for their arrest — facts and circumstances strong enough in themselves to support the belief that they are guilty of a crime that in fact happened. Quite obviously, this has not been met.

claims.excerpt: In People v. Inting,42 we emphasized the important features of the constitutional mandate: (a) The determination of probable cause is a function of the judge; it is not for the provincial fiscal or prosecutor to ascertain. Only the judge and the judge alone makes this determination; (b) The preliminary inquiry made by a prosecutor does not bind the judge. It merely assists him in making the determination of probable cause. The judge does not have to follow what the prosecutor presents to him. By itself, the prosecutor's certification of probable cause is ineffectual. It is the report, the affidavits, the transcript of stenographic notes (if any), and all other supporting documents behind the prosecutor's certification which are material in assisting the judge in his determination of probable cause; and, (c) Judges and prosecutors alike should distinguish the preliminary inquiry which determines probable cause for the issuance of a warrant of arrest from the preliminary investigation proper which ascertains whether the offender should be held for trial or released. Even if the two inquiries be conducted in the course of one and the same proceeding, there should be no confusion about their objectives. The determination of probable cause for the warrant is made by the judge. The preliminary investigation proper — whether or not there is reasonable ground to believe that the accused is guilty of the offense charged and therefore, whether or not he should be subjected to the expense, rigors and embarrassment of trial — is a function of the prosecutor.

From the gathering of evidence until the termination of the preliminary investigation, it appears that the state prosecutors were overly eager to file the case and secure a warrant for the arrest of the accused without bail and their consequent detention. claims.excerpt: The purpose of a preliminary investigation is to secure the innocent against hasty, malicious and oppressive prosecution, and to protect him from an open and public accusation of crime, from the trouble, expense and anxiety of a public trial, and also to protect the state from useless and expensive trial (Trocio v. Manta, 118 SCRA 241, citing Hashim v. Boncan, 71 Phil. 216). The right to a preliminary investigation is a statutory grant, and to withhold it would be to transgress constitutional due process (People v. Oandasa, 25 SCRA 277). However, in order to satisfy the due process clause it is not enough that the preliminary investigation is conducted in the sense of making sure that the transgressor shall not escape with impunity. A preliminary investigation serves not only for the purposes of the State. More importantly, it is a part of the guarantees of freedom and fair play which are birthrights of all who live in the country. It is therefore imperative upon the fiscal or the judge as the case may be, to relieve the accused from the pain of going thru a trial once it is ascertained that the evidence is insufficient to sustain a prima facie case or that no probable cause exists to form a sufficient belief as to the guilt of the accused (emphasis supplied).

Umbal's sworn statement is laden with inconsistencies and improbabilities. Bato's counter-affidavit was considered without giving petitioners the opportunity to refute the same. The PACC which gathered the evidence appears to have had a hand in the determination of probable cause in the preliminary inquiry as the undated resolution of the panel not only bears the letterhead of PACC but was also recommended for approval by the head of the PACC Task Force. Then petitioners were given the runaround in securing a copy of the resolution and the information against them.

claims.excerpt: The purpose of a preliminary investigation is to secure the innocent against hasty, malicious and oppressive prosecution, and to protect him from an open and public accusation of crime, from the trouble, expense and anxiety of a public trial, and also to protect the state from useless and expensive trial (Trocio v. Manta, 118 SCRA 241, citing Hashim v. Boncan, 71 Phil. 216). The right to a preliminary investigation is a statutory grant, and to withhold it would be to transgress constitutional due process (People v. Oandasa, 25 SCRA 277). However, in order to satisfy the due process clause it is not enough that the preliminary investigation is conducted in the sense of making sure that the transgressor shall not escape with impunity. A preliminary investigation serves not only for the purposes of the State. More importantly, it is a part of the guarantees of freedom and fair play which are birthrights of all who live in the country. It is therefore imperative upon the fiscal or the judge as the case may be, to relieve the accused from the pain of going thru a trial once it is ascertained that the evidence is insufficient to sustain a prima facie case or that no probable cause exists to form a sufficient belief as to the guilt of the accused (emphasis supplied).
